title_orig: رسالة عبد الله بن إسمعيل الهاشمي إلى عبد المسيح بن إسحق الكندي يدعوه بها إلى الإسلام ورسالة الكندي إلى الهاشمي يرد بها عليه، ويدعوه إلى النصرانية
title_es: Apología de al-Kindi (carta de al-Hāšimī y respuesta de al-Kindī)
title_en: The Apology of Al Kindy (Risalat ʿAbd al-Masih al-Kindi)
date: c. 9th century (Muir 1882: c. 830 A.D.; OpenITI header: 'second half of 9th C', citing P.S. van Koningsveld 2004)
genre: Epistolary apologetic debate (two letters: Muslim letter of al-Hashimi and Christian reply attributed to al-Kindi)
edition_original: (a) OpenITI 0300Anonymous.RisalataHashimiWaKindi.Kalema00001-ara1 (transcription from alkalema.net; used for all quotations, checked with oilib.verify). (b) archive.org item AlKindi_201306, 1885 printing (OCR; poor for the first pages; used only to cross-check the key sentence). (c) OpenITI SyriacStudies00001 variant (different transcription).
edition_english: William Muir, The Apology of Al Kindy, written at the court of Al Mâmûn (A.H. 215; A.D. 830) ... with an essay on its age and authorship. London: Smith, Elder & Co., 1882.
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/apologyofalkindy00abdarich (djvu text read; book pp. 9-10 checked as page image, PDF page 46)
licence: Archive item shows no open licence. The 1882 title page carries the printed notice '[All Rights Reserved.]'. My judgement: public domain (1882 publication; Muir died 1905), but this is not stated on the scan.
authenticity_note: Attribution to al-Kindi and the date are disputed. The Arabic text is a literary construct in letters. I did not read Muir's essay or van Koningsveld (2004); I only read the OpenITI header that cites van Koningsveld.
notes: Muir's English has an OCR-clear sentence on book pp. 9-10 about Aisha; Muir flags the Safwan story (Arabic p. 60, lines 4 and 6 per his footnote) as objectionable and does not quote the Arabic. The Christian voice ('your companion' = Muhammad) starts after the Quran 33:37 quotation about Zaynab. Muir's enumeration of wives omits the names Khadija and Aisha; his count '(fifteen wives and two slave-girls)' is retained.
